It was being absorbed by what looked like a chunk of an old rag. It seemed that at some point, Leon had tried to insulate the wrist by ramming the rag around it between skin and cuff. The fabric looked charred in spots. It was hard to tell if the effort had helped at all. He winced as the skin seemed to break open more with his fussing, but the more damaged key was refusing to seat properly. Rusted. Swollen. Bits of reddish metal flaked off as he tried to get it into position, the pin of the key threatening to bend under the effort. Frustrated, he slammed it down on a nearby gurney and lined up the second key. Down the hall, a generator flared to life with a roar that scattered nearby crows into a frenzy. Small, rapid footsteps hurried in his direction. Jake was still hunched beside him, trying to coax the second key into the lock. His hands were shaking now — not fear, just urgency; too much adrenaline and too little margin for error. The first key hadn’t made it. This one had to. Meg skidded into the doorway, catching herself just short of a full slide across the dust and broken cement. “We only need one more,” she gasped, hopeful. “It’s going to need to be one of the three.” Jake didn’t even look up. “Help me. Get in here and brace him a bit — he’s pulling the cuff down too hard. I can’t get the lock lined up.” Meg blinked — surprise flashing through the exhaustion. “You found the keys?” “No time. Get him steady.” She dropped to her knees, all motion, all hands. Leon didn’t react at first — just swayed slightly as she caught under his arms, gently lifting his torso up enough to ease the weight off the chain. His eyes fluttered, his head slumping sideways with a relieved sigh as the tension came off the dislocated shoulder. Jake hissed a quiet “C’mon...” through his teeth, twisting the key again. He felt the pin resist, then shift — metal scraping metal — before the cuff clicked open with a tired little pop. He let out a relieved chuckle, pulling the cuff free from the damaged skin. No longer pinned above him, Leon’s arm fell heavily against Meg. The shoulder was at an angry angle, wrist raw and bleeding sluggishly, fierce red marks snaking up the arm and across his neck like lightning. His head lolled against her shoulder, no resistance left to even try lifting it. “Jesus...” Meg breathed, quiet now. Alarm tucked deep behind her voice. “How many times did he even get hit?” Jake was already moving to stabilize him, pushing gear aside to reach Leon’s other side. “I lost track after eight,” he muttered, still rushing. “There were more. I know there were more.” “I heard at least two after we left...” she said, shifting to cradle more of the weight. “Good grief, Leon. How the fuck are you even alive?” His chest hitched a couple of times in what could have been a chuckle, one hand trying to grip at her pant leg to pull himself upright to no success. “’m mag’c.” His head drooped, eyes fluttering lightly, and Jake quickly scooped an arm around his injured side to brace the weight as the two of them fought to get him mobile. “Hey,” Jake said gently, ducking under Leon’s arm to help lift him. “No naps yet, man. We gotta move.” Jake hauled Leon out through the doorway with Meg’s help, dragging him clear of the sparking echo-chamber as fast as they could manage. The Doctor’s footsteps were gone, but Jake didn’t trust the silence. Not with how well the bastard could double back. Leon didn’t fight the movement. Didn’t offer very much help either. Just groaned once — low and thin — as they got him moving, leaning heavily between them as he fought to keep his legs moving. Roughly 4 hallways from that cursed room, his vision started smearing again. His head kept dropping forward, as if he was fighting sleep. He made a soft distressed sound, trying to shift weight to get the others to stop. Just wait for a moment. Let him rest. Stop the world from bleeding color in odd directions. Jake planted a hand on his chest to keep him upright, sharing a look with Meg. “Hey. Stay with me. Talk to me. Are you ok?” He tried... He dragged in a shaking inhale, words delayed, the hallway around him shifting in stuttering lurches. The hallway tilted around him, the lights above pulsing in double-exposure. His legs were still moving, but he couldn’t feel the floor anymore. “I... I don’t... feel—” He swallowed hard, forcing the rest out. “I think I’m— I think—” Another tremor hit — small, sharp — surging through his neck and chest like a loose wire sparking inside him. His breath stuttered. “I—wait— I can’t—” His whole face drained out at once, the sentence caught in a broken half-syllable that never finishes, and in that instant, he dropped, head slumping down, chin hitting chest. Jake and Meg nearly fell under the sudden deadweight as his knees gave out under him, Meg squeaking with surprise as she tried to stand fully upright against the pull. A nearby waiting room would have to serve for a break, and they manhandled Leon down to the floor, leaning him back against a dusty seat that provided at least a bare minimum of cover from being spotted from the doorways. His head lolled back against the seat, unfocused slivers of blue barely visible through lightly twitching eyelids.
